subject: Deal onramp & capacity playbook for Orbitium - options and ramp schedule
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@orbitium.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deal onramp & capacity playbook for Orbitium - options and ramp schedule

Hi Alex,

Following our call this morning — attached are three proposed reservation lanes for Orbitium that map to expected go-to-market velocity. The sheet (Orbitium_capacity_options_v1.xlsx) includes modeled token throughput, estimated monthly spend, and activation credits. High level options:

- Option A — Lean onramp (conservative): 16 GPU minimum guarantee, 32 GPU committed cluster with burst to 64 for 90 days. Fastest near-term cost-saver but riskier if traffic grows faster than forecast.
- Option B — Balanced ramp (recommended): 32 GPU minimum guarantee, 64 GPU committed cluster. 3-month ramp (32 → 48 → 64) with pre-warm windows and a 2-week canary at 30% traffic.
- Option C — Growth-first (aggressive): 64 GPU minimum, 128 GPU cluster with staged activation across first 60 days and higher committed discounts.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm target 95th percentile latency SLO (we assumed 120ms p95 on chat endpoints).
- Confirm whether procurement needs staggered billing or a single reserved contract.

We also attached a draft SOW (SOW-draft-Orbitium.pdf) with onboarding milestones and activation credits you can share with procurement. If you prefer, we can start Option B but with a contract that allows stepping down to Option A within 60 days if traffic stays low (commercial guardrails included).

Next steps: pick an option and we’ll produce a carve-out pricing sheet and activation runbook.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan — I agree we should avoid exposing the customer to availability risk by letting them start too low. Commercial approach I recommend:

- Offer a staged guarantee: Month 1 = 24 GPU min, Month 2 = 32 GPU min, Month 3+ = 48–64 depending on usage bands. This sits between their ask and our risk tolerance.
- Provide a 10% activation credit applied to month 1 and month 2 billing if p95 latency stays within the agreed SLOs.
- Include a clear rollback clause: if p95 degrades >25% vs baseline for two consecutive days we immediately reduce production traffic to the canary endpoint and pause further activation.

Karthik — please confirm the technical thresholds (we need concrete numbers for the SOW). I can present the commercial staircase to procurement and fold in a small ramp credit to get the signature.

Thanks,

Marissa / Jordan — technical confirmation and suggested activation runbook below. Attaching activation_runbook_v1.md as a reference (see attachments).

Assumptions:
- Model: 70B chat model running fp16 quantized weights on A100-80GB (we can convert to 4-bit quant later if they accept quality tradeoffs).
- Baseline traffic profile (from Alex's projection): 4k p50 requests/day initially with 10–12 tokens per request average.

Sizing and thresholds:
- Minimum baseline we recommend: 32 GPUs (A100-80GB) to maintain KV cache hit rates and <120ms p95 for chat endpoint under expected concurrency. 24 GPUs would have a tight cache warm-up and higher cold p95.
- Canary: route 30% of traffic to a single primary endpoint (chat-v1-canary) for 14 days. Collect per-request latency, model-quality regression checks (top-N similarity), and tail error rate.
- Warm-up: pre-warm KV cache for 48–72 hours using a staged warm-up (replay subset of production prompts).
- Autoscale/burst: allow ephemeral burst lanes up to +50% of cluster capacity using burst credits for one-off spikes.

Rollback triggers (automated):
- If p95 > 1.5x baseline for 2 consecutive hours OR
- If model-quality regression > 3% on evaluation prompt set (we'll ship a 500-prompt suite) OR
- If GPU utilization > 85% sustained for 30+ minutes without expected traffic spike
Then: automatic route 100% of traffic away from new cluster, initiate failover to fallback model variant, and page on-call infra + ML eng.

Recommended commercial mapping (aligns with Marissa):
- Month 1: 32 GPU guarantee (we'll allow 24 for an initial 7-day ramp with pre-warm but billing credited to 32 if they exercise the credit).
- Month 2: step to 48 GPU guarantee conditioned on canary success and traffic growth.

I'll be available to join the call with Orbitium procurement if they want to walk through the runbook.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Orbitium capacity path — agreed recommendation & next steps (ORBT-2027-1123)

Alex — thanks for the quick responses and for looping procurement. After internal review (Marissa + Karthik), here’s the path we propose and what we’ll put into the SOW for signature: 

1) Commercial & capacity commitment
- Month 1: 32 GPU min (with a technical allowance to start at 24 for up to 7 days while we pre-warm; billing will be at 32 but we’ll apply a 10% activation credit to month 1).
- Month 2: step to 48 GPU min conditioned on canary success. Month 3+: move to 64 GPU cluster if usage justifies.

2) Technical onramp
- 14-day canary on a single chat endpoint at 30% traffic.
- 48–72 hour pre-warm run to populate KV caches using replayed prompts.
- Rollback & alerting per the thresholds Karthik outlined (p95, quality regression, sustained GPU util).

3) Deliverables & timing
- We’ll share a final SOW with these terms and the activation schedule by EOD tomorrow. DocuSign link will be included and HubSpot deal updated (link below).
- Karthik will run the technical onboarding checklist and coordinate pre-warm windows with your infra team.

If that sounds good, procurement / legal can expect the SOW + DocuSign this week and we’ll target a 2027-05-03 production activation (subject to signed SOW and pre-warm window).
